ours.value: Unrestricted (a,b) and(-a,-b) yield exactly the same squared path for every real m; simultaneously changing both twin loadings also preserves their products. Each independent ACE component has this global sign symmetry. Conversely if squared affine paths agree at three distinct moderator values, their degree-at-most-two difference is identically zero. Factoring it implies the paths are identical or globally negative. With strictly positive intercepts only the identical solution remains. Existing exact midpoint witness 9/25 versus1/100 shows the binary reflection generally fails between endpoints.

ours.value: Fix M=m and abbreviate exp(beta0a+beta1a*m)=A, similarly C,E. Under the stated independent innovations, MZ traits equal mu+beta1m*m+U_C+U_A+U_Ej, with innovation variances C,A,E. Hence both means are mu+beta1m*m, both variances T=A+C+E, and covariance K_MZ=A+C. For DZ, Eq5.12 gives a shared genetic innovation of variance1/2 and Eq5.13 adds an independent individual innovation of variance1/2. Multiplying by sqrt(A) in Eq5.14 gives each genetic variance A and cross-twin genetic covariance A/2. Adding the common C and independent E innovations yields the same mean and T, and K_DZ=A/2+C. This also verifies the inverse identities A=2*(K_MZ-K_DZ), C=2*K_DZ-K_MZ, E=T-K_MZ already independently symbolically checked.

claims.methods: The source free-common-mean assumption is confirmed by the saved independent source audit: mu is a fitted parameter; setting mu=0 in data generation is not a fitted constraint. The existing all-zero-response argument shows likelihood strictly improves as free mu decreases and tends to supremum1 without attainment. It is a valid counterexample to universal existence of a finite MLE, including when both zygosities and both moderator levels are represented. The example does not produce two local or global maxima. If only one maximum is read as at most one when one exists, no counterexample to that claim has been supplied. The independently reviewed joint-item argument establishes population parameter injectivity under known finite positive logistic calibrations, two distinct conditionally independent observations, positive Gaussian ACE components, observed moments and joint zygosity/moderator support. Together with correct specification this yields a unique population expected-log-likelihood maximizer via KL divergence. It does not yield finite-likelihood concavity or global uniqueness.
